API endpoint functions for direct data access

import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

The client exposes one typed function per API endpoint. Use these to build custom flows or to fetch data outside the components. Parameters are camelCase here and snake_case on the wire. Response objects keep the API's snake_case field names.

For request and response schemas, see the [Zocdoc API Reference](https://api-docs.zocdoc.com/apis). For how the calls fit together, see [Find Provider Availability and Book Appointments](https://api-docs.zocdoc.com/guides/patient/book-appointments).

## Provider Search

### searchProviderLocations

`GET /v1/provider_locations`: search for provider locations near a ZIP code.

```typescript
import { searchProviderLocations } from '@zocdoc/api-components';

const result = await searchProviderLocations({
  zipCode: '11201',
  specialtyId: 'sp_153',
  insurancePlanId: 'ip_9111',
});

// result.providerLocations: ProviderLocation[]
// result.totalCount: number
// result.pageSize: number
// result.searchParameters: the filters the API applied, including defaults
```

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `zipCode` | `string` | Yes | 5-digit ZIP code. The API has no "search everywhere" mode |
| `specialtyId` | `string` | No | Filter by specialty |
| `visitReasonId` | `string` | No | Filter by visit reason |
| `insurancePlanId` | `string` | No | Only providers in-network for this plan |
| `visitType` | `'all' \| 'in_person' \| 'video_visit'` | No | In-person, video, or both |
| `maxDistanceToPatientMi` | `number` | No | Search radius in miles |
| `page` | `number` | No | Zero-based page index |
| `pageSize` | `number` | No | Results per page (default: `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE`, 10) |

A search that matches nothing resolves with an empty `providerLocations` array. It doesn't throw.

Some provider locations include `booking_requirements`, such as insurance member and plan IDs that are required to book. Check these before collecting patient details.

## Availability

### getAvailability

`GET /v1/provider_locations/availability`: open timeslots for one or more provider locations.

```typescript
import { getAvailability } from '@zocdoc/api-components';

const entries = await getAvailability({
  providerLocationIds: ['pr_abc|lo_xyz'],
  visitReasonId: 'pc_FRO-18leckytNKtruw5dLR',
  patientType: 'new',
  startDate: '2026-10-07',
  endDate: '2026-10-13',
});

// entries: ProviderLocationAvailability[], one per requested location
// entries[0].timeslots: AvailabilitySlot[] (always an array, possibly empty)
```

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `providerLocationIds` | `string[]` | Yes | `pr_…\|lo_…` IDs, passed through unchanged. Batch several locations in one call |
| `visitReasonId` | `string` | Yes | Availability differs by visit reason |
| `patientType` | `'new' \| 'existing'` | Yes | Availability differs for new and existing patients |
| `startDate` | `string` | No | `YYYY-MM-DD` in provider local time. Defaults to today |
| `endDate` | `string` | No | `YYYY-MM-DD`. Defaults to 7 days after the start, and must be within 30 days of it |
| `insurancePlanId` | `string` | No | Insurance plan ID |
| `insuranceCarrierId` | `string` | No | Insurance carrier ID |

<Aside>
  The API rejects windows longer than 30 days, and Zocdoc guarantees availability only up to 150 days out. The client exports the 30-day limit as `MAX_AVAILABILITY_DAYS` so you can clamp windows to it.
</Aside>

## Appointments

### createAppointment

`POST /v1/appointments`: book a timeslot.

```typescript
import { createAppointment } from '@zocdoc/api-components';

const appointment = await createAppointment({
  providerLocationId: 'pr_abc|lo_xyz',
  visitReasonId: 'pc_FRO-18leckytNKtruw5dLR',
  startTime: slot.start_time, // Exactly as returned by getAvailability
  patientType: 'new',
  patient: {
    first_name: 'Test',
    last_name: 'Patient',
    date_of_birth: '1990-01-15',
    sex_at_birth: 'female',
    phone_number: '2125550001',
    email_address: 'test@example.com',
    patient_address: {
      address1: '1 Test St',
      city: 'Brooklyn',
      state: 'NY',
      zip_code: '11201',
    },
    insurance: { is_self_pay: true },
  },
});

// appointment.appointment_id: string
// appointment.appointment_status: 'confirmed' | 'pending_booking' | 'booking_failed' | ...
```

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `providerLocationId` | `string` | Yes | Provider location ID |
| `visitReasonId` | `string` | Yes | Visit reason ID |
| `startTime` | `string` | Yes | A `start_time` from `getAvailability`, unchanged, offset included |
| `patientType` | `'new' \| 'existing'` | Yes | Must match the availability you searched |
| `patient` | `Patient` | Yes | Patient details. Every field is PHI |
| `notes` | `string` | No | Patient-written note, maximum 100 characters. Also PHI |

`phone_number` must be 10 digits with no formatting, and the 1st and 4th digits can't be `0` or `1`.

<Aside type="caution">
  A resolved promise doesn't mean a confirmed appointment. Check `appointment_status`, since `pending_booking` and `booking_failed` both arrive on a successful response. See [Booking Failures on a Success Status](/zocdoc-api-components/client/errors/#booking-failures-on-a-success-status).
</Aside>

Use `appointment_id` to reschedule or cancel. See Zocdoc's [Reschedule](https://api-docs.zocdoc.com/guides/patient/reschedule-appointments) and [Cancel](https://api-docs.zocdoc.com/guides/patient/cancel-appointments) guides. The client doesn't wrap those endpoints yet. To hear about status changes, such as a pending booking becoming confirmed, subscribe your backend to Zocdoc [Webhooks](https://api-docs.zocdoc.com/guides/webhooks).

## Reference Data

Specialties, visit reasons, and insurance plans supply the IDs the other endpoints take. See Zocdoc's [Reference Data](https://api-docs.zocdoc.com/guides/reference-data) guide. Each function fetches every page and returns the complete list.

### getSpecialties

`GET /v1/specialties`

```typescript
import { getSpecialties } from '@zocdoc/api-components';

const specialties = await getSpecialties();
// [{ id: 'sp_153', name: 'Primary Care Doctor', default_visit_reason_id: '…', ... }, ...]
```

### getVisitReasons

`GET /v1/visit_reasons`, optionally filtered by specialty:

```typescript
import { getVisitReasons } from '@zocdoc/api-components';

const reasons = await getVisitReasons('sp_153');
// [{ id: 'pc_FRO-18leckytNKtruw5dLR', name: 'New patient visit', specialty_id: 'sp_153' }, ...]
```

### getInsurancePlans

`GET /v1/insurance_plans`, with optional filters:

```typescript
import { getInsurancePlans } from '@zocdoc/api-components';

const plans = await getInsurancePlans({ state: 'NY', careCategory: 'health' });
```

| Filter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `state` | `string` | Two-letter code. Returns plans whose coverage includes the state |
| `careCategory` | `'health' \| 'dental' \| 'vision'` | Plan category |
| `networkType` | `string` | Network type |
| `programType` | `InsuranceProgramType` | For example, `commercial` or `medicare` |
| `status` | `'active' \| 'inactive' \| 'deleted'` | Defaults to `active` on the server |

<Aside type="caution">
  Always filter where you can. The unfiltered production list has more than 10,000 plans. That's dozens of requests and megabytes of JSON to fill one dropdown. `state` is the natural filter for a booking flow.
</Aside>

## Caching

Reference data is cached in memory for the page lifetime. Each distinct set of filters gets its own cache entry. Concurrent callers share one in-flight request, and a failed request isn't cached, so the next call retries.

```typescript
const a = await getSpecialties(); // Network request
const b = await getSpecialties(); // Cached
```

To force a refresh, for example after switching between sandbox and production, call `clearReferenceDataCache()`.

Provider search and availability aren't cached, because they change constantly.

The `<zd-availability-grid>` component displays a day-by-day view of available appointments.

## Usage

### Self-Fetching Mode

Provide IDs and the component fetches availability:

```html preview
<zd-availability-grid
  provider-location-id="pr_abc123-def456_wxyz7890|lo_abc123-def456_wxyz7890"
  visit-reason-id="pc_FRO-18leckytNKtruw5dLR"
  days="7"
></zd-availability-grid>
```

While a range loads, the pager stays visible and each date cell becomes a full-cell skeleton with a shimmer. The loading status is announced to assistive technology, and the animation adapts to reduced-motion preferences.

### Batched Data Mode

When a parent has already fetched availability, assign its slots through the `timeslots` JavaScript property. This example builds dates relative to today so the slots remain inside the grid's visible week:

```html preview
<zd-availability-grid id="batched-grid" days="7"></zd-availability-grid>
<script>
  const dateFromToday = (offset) => {
    const date = new Date();
    date.setDate(date.getDate() + offset);
    const year = date.getFullYear();
    const month = String(date.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, '0');
    const day = String(date.getDate()).padStart(2, '0');
    return `${year}-${month}-${day}`;
  };

  document.getElementById('batched-grid').timeslots = [
    { start_time: `${dateFromToday(0)}T09:00:00-04:00`, booking_url: null },
    { start_time: `${dateFromToday(1)}T10:30:00-04:00`, booking_url: null },
    { start_time: `${dateFromToday(1)}T14:00:00-04:00`, booking_url: null },
  ];
</script>
```

`timeslots` is a JavaScript property, not an HTML attribute. An empty array means the parent supplied availability with no slots; leave it `undefined` when the grid should fetch for itself.

## Attributes

| Attribute              | Type      | Default | Description                                           |
| ---------------------- | --------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `provider-location-id` | `string`  | —       | Provider location to fetch for                        |
| `visit-reason-id`      | `string`  | —       | Visit reason required for fetching                    |
| `patient-type`         | `string`  | `new`   | Patient type for availability                         |
| `loading`              | `boolean` | `false` | Show placeholders while the host loads supplied slots |
| `start-date`           | `string`  | today   | First day in the visible range                        |
| `days`                 | `number`  | `14`    | Number of days to show (max 30)                       |
| `selected-day`         | `string`  | —       | Selected day as `YYYY-MM-DD`                          |
| `show-more`            | `boolean` | `false` | Show the "More" control                               |
| `hide-window`          | `boolean` | `false` | Hide the range header and its pager                   |

### JavaScript Properties

| Property    | Type                          | Description                                     |
| ----------- | ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `timeslots` | `readonly AvailabilitySlot[]` | Pre-fetched slots; setting it disables fetching |

## Events

| Event                | Detail                         | Description        |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------ |
| `day-select`         | `{ day, providerLocationId? }` | Day clicked        |
| `window-change`      | `{ startDate, endDate }`       | Date range shifted |
| `more-select`        | `{}`                           | "More" clicked     |
| `availability-error` | `{ error }`                    | Fetch failed       |

## Accessibility

- Days are buttons with date labels
- Available count announced per day
- Arrow keys navigate between days

## Styling

The grid uses a seven-column layout that adapts to its container. Day cells inherit the host text color and use the Zocdoc design tokens for available and unavailable states.

The `<zd-patient-form>` component collects required patient information for booking an appointment.

## Usage

```html preview
<zd-patient-form></zd-patient-form>
```

## Fields

The form collects:

- First name
- Last name
- Date of birth
- Sex at birth
- Phone number
- Email address
- Address (street, city, state, ZIP)
- Notes (optional)

## Events

| Event | Detail | Description |
|-------|--------|-------------|
| `patient-submit` | `PatientData` | Form submitted with valid data |

The event detail contains all patient fields. **This is PHI** — only send it to your configured Zocdoc `baseUrl`.

## Accessibility

- All fields have visible labels
- Required fields marked with asterisk and `aria-required`
- Validation errors linked via `aria-describedby`
- Related fields grouped in fieldsets (e.g., address)

## Validation

Client-side validation runs on submit:

- Required fields must be filled
- Email must be valid format
- Phone must be 10 digits
- Date of birth must be valid and in the past

Server-side validation may return additional errors, displayed inline.

## Styling

| CSS Property | Default | Description |
|--------------|---------|-------------|
| `--zd-form-gap` | `1rem` | Spacing between fields |
| `--zd-form-label-size` | `0.875rem` | Label font size |

## Props Down, Events Up

All Zocdoc API Components follow a strict unidirectional data flow:

- **Properties flow down** — Parent components pass data to children via attributes and properties
- **Events flow up** — Children emit custom events to notify parents of user actions or state changes

There is no shared state container, no context protocol, and no global store. Each component is self-contained.

## Component Hierarchy

<ComponentHierarchy />

The `<zd-booking>` component listens for events from its children and updates their properties in response. You can replicate this wiring yourself for custom flows.

## Standalone Capability

Every child component works without its parent. You can render `<zd-provider-card>` by itself, pass it a provider object, and it renders correctly. Components never reach upward for context or depend on a specific parent.

This enables:

- **Testing in isolation** — Unit test any component without mounting the full tree
- **Custom compositions** — Mix and match components in layouts we didn't anticipate
- **Progressive enhancement** — Start with `<zd-booking>` and decompose later if needed

## Event Types

Each component exports TypeScript types for its events:

```typescript
import type { ZdProviderSearchEvents, DetailOf } from '@zocdoc/api-components';

element.addEventListener('provider-results', (event: DetailOf<ZdProviderSearchEvents['provider-results']>) => {
  const { providers, totalCount } = event.detail;
});
```

## No Global State

The components don't use Redux, MobX, signals, or any state management library. State lives in:

1. **Component properties** — The source of truth for what a component displays
2. **Component internal state** — Managed by Lit's reactive properties
3. **Your application** — If you need cross-component state, manage it yourself and pass it down

This makes components predictable and easy to integrate into any framework.

These components are a UI layer over the [Zocdoc public API](https://api-docs.zocdoc.com/guides). They implement Zocdoc's **availability search and patient booking** integration path. This page covers the parts of the API that shape your integration, and links to Zocdoc's guides for the details.

## How the Booking Flow Maps to the API

Zocdoc's [Find Provider Availability and Book Appointments](https://api-docs.zocdoc.com/guides/patient/book-appointments) guide describes a sequence of calls. Each step maps to a client function and the components involved:

| Step | API endpoint | Client function | Fetched by | Rendered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Load search options | `GET /v1/specialties`, `GET /v1/visit_reasons`, `GET /v1/insurance_plans` | `getSpecialties`, `getVisitReasons`, `getInsurancePlans` | `<zd-provider-search>` | `<zd-provider-search>` |
| Find providers | `GET /v1/provider_locations` | `searchProviderLocations` | `<zd-provider-search>` | `<zd-provider-results>`, `<zd-provider-card>` |
| Show open times | `GET /v1/provider_locations/availability` | `getAvailability` | `<zd-booking>` | `<zd-availability-picker>`, `<zd-availability-grid>` |
| Book | `POST /v1/appointments` | `createAppointment` | `<zd-booking>` | `<zd-patient-form>` |
| Confirm | (booking response) | — | — | `<zd-booking-confirmation>` |

`<zd-booking>` runs every step in order. If you compose the components yourself, your code makes the availability and booking calls and passes the results down as properties. See [Composed vs Single Element](/zocdoc-api-components/guides/composed-vs-single/).

## Rules the API Enforces

The components already follow these rules. You'll need them if you call the client functions directly.

### Provider search

- `zip_code` is required. There's no "search everywhere" mode.
- Results are paged (`page`, `page_size`; the default page size is 10).
- Provider location IDs are literal `pr_…|lo_…` pairs. Pass them through unchanged.

### Availability

- Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD` in the provider's local time.
- The start date defaults to today, and the end date defaults to 7 days later.
- The end date **must be within 30 days** of the start. The client exports this limit as `MAX_AVAILABILITY_DAYS`.
- Zocdoc guarantees availability up to **150 days out**. Later dates may be accepted but aren't supported.
- `patient_type` (`new` or `existing`) and `visit_reason_id` are required. Availability depends on both.

### Booking

- `start_time` must exactly match a timeslot returned by availability, offset included.
- **A successful response doesn't mean a confirmed appointment.** Check `appointment_status`. It may be `confirmed`, `pending_booking` (waiting on the practice), or `booking_failed`, which is a failure that arrives with a `200` status.
- Some provider locations have booking requirements. For example, insurance member and plan IDs may be required, self-pay may not be accepted, or the location may be in-network only. Violating a requirement returns `400`.
- `notes` is limited to 100 characters.
- To reschedule or cancel an appointment, use the returned `appointment_id`. See Zocdoc's [Reschedule](https://api-docs.zocdoc.com/guides/patient/reschedule-appointments) and [Cancel](https://api-docs.zocdoc.com/guides/patient/cancel-appointments) guides. The components don't cover these flows yet.

<Aside type="note">
  Instead of booking through the API, you can send the patient to the `booking_url` on a timeslot to complete booking on zocdoc.com. Zocdoc notes this only suits certain use cases and partnerships. See the [FAQs](https://api-docs.zocdoc.com/guides/faqs).
</Aside>

## Reference Data

Specialties, visit reasons, and insurance plans are Zocdoc-specific IDs that other endpoints require. They're described in Zocdoc's [Reference Data](https://api-docs.zocdoc.com/guides/reference-data) guide. Visit reasons can be filtered by specialty. The sandbox comes pre-populated with sample records.

The client caches each list for the page lifetime. Filter insurance plans by `state` where you can, because the unfiltered production list has more than 10,000 entries. See [Endpoints](/zocdoc-api-components/client/endpoints/#reference-data).

## Rate Limits and Performance

From Zocdoc's [Performance](https://api-docs.zocdoc.com/guides/performance) guide:

- Requests over the rate limit return **`429`**. Zocdoc doesn't publish the numbers, and limits can be lowered without notice to prevent abuse or raised for high-traffic apps.
- Back off **exponentially** when you get a `429`. See [Retry Logic](/zocdoc-api-components/client/errors/#retry-logic).
- Gzip compression is supported for both requests and responses. Browsers send `Accept-Encoding: gzip` automatically.

## Data Handling

Patient details sent to `POST /v1/appointments` are protected health information. The components send them only to the configured `baseUrl`. They never log them or include them in error messages. If you use `createAppointment` or listen to component events directly, follow the same rules: log actions, not field values.

  type="email"

```html preview

  <zd-menu-item>Duplicate</zd-menu-item>
  <zd-menu-item>Archive</zd-menu-item>
</zd-menu>
```

### Grouped choices

```html preview
<zd-menu placement="bottom-start">
  <zd-button slot="trigger" variant="secondary">Display options</zd-button>
  <zd-menu-group heading="Density" select="single">
    <zd-menu-item>Comfortable</zd-menu-item>
    <zd-menu-item>Compact</zd-menu-item>
  </zd-menu-group>
</zd-menu>
```

<zd-tabs layout="vertical">

></zd-text-area>

<zd-text-area label="Reason for request" name="reason" required invalid
